title: Modular kitchen cost in Mumbai: a 2026 price guide
desc: What a modular kitchen really costs in Mumbai, Thane and Navi Mumbai — price per sq ft, what changes the price, and how to save without cutting corners.
body: Most families in Mumbai spend between ₹1.5 lakh and ₹3 lakh on a modular kitchen for a typical 1BHK or 2BHK flat. The price depends far more on the materials and hardware you pick than on the size of the kitchen.
Kitchen makers usually price cabinets per square foot of shutter area (the front surface you see). In Mumbai and Thane in 2026, expect roughly:
A standard L-shaped kitchen in a 2BHK has about 90–120 sq ft of shutter area including lofts, which is how most kitchens end up in the ₹1.5–3 lakh range.
Board: waterproof BWP plywood costs more than BWR or MDF, but lasts much longer under the sink.
Hardware: soft-close hinges and drawer channels, tandem boxes and corner units can add ₹20,000–₹60,000.
Shutter finish: acrylic and PU cost more than laminate and need more care.
Countertop: granite is usually separate from the carpentry price.
Lofts and tall units: extra storage adds area and therefore cost.
Use BWP plywood only for the sink base and BWR for the rest.
Choose laminate shutters — they are tough and easy to clean.
Spend on good hinges and channels rather than on fancy handles.
Hire on labour basis if you can buy the material yourself.
Questions to ask before you order
Which brand and grade of plywood and laminate will be used?
Which hinge and channel brand, and is it soft-close?
Is the countertop, sink and chimney cut-out included?
What is the warranty on workmanship?

title: Wardrobe cost per sq ft in Mumbai (sliding, hinged and loft)
desc: How much a made-to-measure wardrobe costs per sq ft in Mumbai and Thane, how to calculate the area, and which finish and hardware to choose.
body: A carpenter-made wardrobe in Mumbai usually costs ₹1,200 to ₹2,200 per square foot of front area. A typical 7 ft × 7 ft bedroom wardrobe therefore costs about ₹60,000 to ₹1 lakh including the loft.
Multiply the width by the height of the wardrobe front. A wardrobe 6 ft wide and 7 ft high is 42 sq ft. Add the loft separately — a 6 ft × 2 ft loft adds 12 sq ft.
Hinged doors cost less and open the full wardrobe at once — good when there is space in front.
Sliding doors save space in small bedrooms and look modern, but the track needs good quality.
A mirror on a sliding door saves buying a separate dressing mirror.
Hanging space at least 3.5 ft high for shirts and 5 ft for long clothes.
Two or three drawers with good channels.
A locker drawer if you need one.
Shelves 12–14 inches apart so piles don't topple.

title: Contract basis vs labour basis: which is better for your interior work?
desc: The difference between hiring an interior team on contract basis and labour basis, the real savings, and the risks of each.
body: When you hire carpenters in Mumbai you can usually choose between two ways of paying: contract basis, where the team supplies material and labour for one price, and labour basis, where you buy the material and pay only for the work.
One price for everything — material, labour, hardware, finishing and fitting.
Less running around for you; the team buys and transports the material.
Easier to compare quotes and plan your budget.
Best when you are busy, or when the job is large such as a full flat.
You buy plywood, laminate, hardware and other material yourself.
You pay the team per sq ft or per day for the work — often ₹250 – ₹450 per sq ft for wardrobes and kitchens.
You control the brands and can save the dealer margin.
Best when you know materials well or have time to visit shops.

Labour basis can save 10–15% if you buy material at a good rate and nothing is wasted. But wrong quantities, extra trips and delays can wipe out the saving. For small jobs labour basis is often cheaper; for complete flats contract basis is usually simpler and safer.
Get the scope, brands and payment schedule in writing.
Pay in stages linked to work done, not all in advance.
Check one completed site of the team before you hire them.
We work both ways. Tell us about your job and we will quote on contract basis, labour basis or both, so you can compare.

title: 2BHK interior cost in Mumbai and Thane: what to budget
desc: A practical budget for 2BHK interiors in Mumbai, Thane and Navi Mumbai — basic, mid-range and premium — with a room-by-room breakdown.
body: Complete interiors for a 2BHK flat in Mumbai or Thane usually cost ₹6 lakh to ₹11 lakh with a carpenter-led team. Designer firms often charge more for the same work.
Basic + false ceiling, beds with storage, shoe rack, pooja unit
Mid-range + wall panelling, sliding wardrobes, acrylic kitchen, lighting

A 2BHK usually takes 30–45 working days on site, depending on the scope and society working hours.
Get society permission and check allowed working hours.

Freeze the design and materials before work begins — changes later cost time and money.

title: Plywood, MDF or solid wood: choosing material for your furniture
desc: Which board or wood to choose for wardrobes, kitchens, beds and sofas in Mumbai's humid climate — BWP, BWR, MDF, teak and sheesham explained.
body: Mumbai's humidity is hard on furniture. Choosing the right material for each piece matters more than any design detail.
BWP (boiling water proof) plywood: best for kitchen sink units and bathroom vanities.
BWR (boiling water resistant) plywood: good for wardrobes, beds and TV units.
Commercial / MR plywood: cheaper, only for dry areas — not recommended for kitchens.
MDF is smooth and good for painted or PU shutters, but it swells if it gets wet. Particle board is the cheapest and is used in ready-made furniture; we avoid it for kitchens and wardrobes.
Teak (sagwan): strong, resists termites and moisture, and ages well — ideal for sofas, beds and doors. It is the most expensive.
Sheesham: hard and handsome with a strong grain — good for beds, dining sets and chairs at a lower price than teak.
Solid wood should be properly seasoned, or it can crack and warp.

title: False ceiling cost in Mumbai: gypsum vs POP
desc: False ceiling prices per sq ft in Mumbai and Thane for 2026, gypsum vs POP, and what to plan for lights, AC ducts and fans before work starts.
body: A false ceiling in Mumbai usually costs ₹90 to ₹160 per square foot of ceiling area, depending on the material and the design.
Gypsum board, simple flat or border
Gypsum boards are factory-made, quick to install and give a clean finish — the common choice today.
POP is made on site, allows curved designs, but takes longer and creates more dust.
Both need a good painter for a smooth finish.
Position of lights, fans and AC units.
Access panels for AC piping and wiring.
